items.title: IS YOUR CHEAP LUGGAGE TOXIC? THE HIDDEN CONCERNS LURKING INSIDE YOUR SUITCASE
items.content:
There is a distinct moment when packing for a long-awaited holiday shifts from excitement to careful preparation.

Flights are booked, itineraries are finalized, and travelers invest in everything from comfortable footwear to premium skincare products. Yet one of the most important travel essentials often receives surprisingly little attention: the suitcase itself.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

According to travel specialists at The Travel Store, many consumers focus heavily on appearance and price while overlooking the materials used inside their luggage:

Why Does Some Luggage Smell So Strong?

If you have ever opened a newly purchased suitcase and noticed a sharp chemical smell, you are not alone.

These odors are often associated with manufacturing materials, including adhesives, coatings, dyes, and synthetic fabrics used during production. Heat can intensify these smells, especially when luggage is left inside a car boot, storage room, or poorly ventilated space.

While the presence of an odor does not automatically indicate a serious health risk, many travelers prefer luggage made with higher-quality materials that minimize unpleasant smells and provide a more comfortable travel experience.

For individuals who are particularly sensitive to strong scents or chemical odors, prolonged exposure in confined spaces may cause discomfort, making material quality an important factor to consider when selecting travel gear.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

More Than Just a Comfort Issue

Beyond material quality, cheaper luggage often faces another challenge: durability.

Frequent travelers know that a suitcase is subjected to considerable stress throughout its lifetime. Wheels encounter uneven surfaces, handles are repeatedly extended and retracted, and luggage shells endure constant impacts during transit.

Lower-quality bags may show signs of wear more quickly, leading many consumers to replace them sooner than expected. This cycle of frequent replacement contributes to unnecessary waste and increased long-term costs.

Brands that prioritize durability, repairability, and long-term performance offer a different approach. Replaceable wheels, serviceable handles, reinforced corners, and durable shell materials can significantly extend a suitcase's lifespan.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

Travel Smarter, Waste Less

As sustainability becomes increasingly important to modern travelers, longevity has become one of the most valuable features a suitcase can offer.

Choosing luggage designed to last for years rather than seasons helps reduce landfill waste while delivering better long-term value. Repairing worn components instead of replacing an entire suitcase can further extend its usefulness.

When a suitcase eventually reaches the end of its journey, recycling or repurposing its materials can help reduce environmental impact and support a more sustainable travel lifestyle.

The Bottom Line

A suitcase does far more than carry your belongings from one destination to another.

The materials inside, the durability of its construction, and its ability to withstand years of travel all play a roles in the overall experience.

Before choosing the cheapest option available, travelers may want to look beyond the price tag and consider what their luggage is made of, how long it is likely to last, and whether it is designed for the journeys still ahead.

items.title: WHY SMART TRAVELLERS ARE EXPLORING KUALA LUMPUR WITH AVIS
items.content:
Kuala Lumpur is one of those cities that rewards travellers who move freely. The best food spots are not always next to the train station. The cafés everyone talks about are hidden inside neighbourhoods. And sometimes, the best part of the trip happens completely outside the itinerary.


Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

And that is exactly why travellers are choosing AVIS when visiting Kuala Lumpur. Because in a city like KL, convenience is not the only thing that matters; freedom matters too.

First-time visitors often assume Kuala Lumpur is easy to explore within just a few train stops or short rides around the city. At first, it feels simple enough.

But after a full day of moving between shopping districts, food streets, attractions, and hotels, travellers quickly realise how spread-out Kuala Lumpur actually is.

Exploring multiple places in one day can become tiring, especially when time, comfort, and flexibility start to matter more.

And that is usually when the experience changes. Because having your own car gives you the freedom to move around the city at your own pace without interruption.


Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

With AVIS, your day no longer revolves around transportation.

You can start your morning at the Petronas Twin Towers, head to Bangsar for brunch, spend the afternoon shopping in Bukit Bintang and still drive out for late-night street food without worrying about finding a ride back.

By all means, no waiting, no surge pricing, no rushing to catch the last train. Just complete flexibility to experience Kuala Lumpur comfortably.

AVIS makes travelling around Kuala Lumpur easier with:

• Reliable and comfortable vehicles

• Easy booking experience

• Flexible vehicle options for solo travellers, couples, families, and groups

• Convenient pick-up locations

• A trusted international brand that travellers already recognise


Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

Most importantly, AVIS gives travellers peace of mind. You land, collect your car and start your journey immediately. No unnecessary complications.

For travellers visiting with family, friends or even for business, that convenience makes a huge difference throughout the trip. Some of the best moments in Kuala Lumpur happen unexpectedly.

Public transportation follows routes, but real travel does not. That is why driving gives travellers a completely different relationship with the city.

You are no longer limited by schedules or locations. You explore because you want to, not because transportation allows you to.

Sometimes the journey itself becomes the best part of the holiday.


Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

With AVIS, travellers get more than just a rental car.

They get the freedom to experience Kuala Lumpur properly, comfortably, confidently and without limits.

If you are planning your next trip to Kuala Lumpur, make every journey smoother with AVIS and discover the city the way modern travellers should. For more details, visit www.avis.com.my

items.title: EXPLORING AUTHENTIC ZAMBIAN FOOD: A CULTURAL LUNCH EXPERIENCE WITH OUR KLTHEGUIDE TEAM
items.content:
There’s a specific kind of magic that happens when an editorial team stops rushing.
Most days behind the KLTG desk, our workspace is a battleground of glowing laptop screens, half-edited drafts of city trails, and half-cold coffees. 

We are constantly chasing the city's pulse.

But today, the frantic rhythm of typing suddenly dissolved, replaced by something deeply grounding: the rich, aromatic steam of an authentic Zambian feast.

We didn’t just take a lunch break.

We flipped open a hidden palate passport and went on an unscripted, one-day culinary travel journey across the globe without leaving our chairs.

Breaking the Bread of Africa

At the absolute center of our table sat a massive, pristine mound of steaming Nshima.

In Zambian culture, Nshima isn't just a side dish; it is the literal and emotional anchor of life.

Made from ground maize white cornmeal that is vigorously whipped into a dense, smooth porridge-like, it holds a comforting heat.

There’s a beautiful, tactile intimacy to eating it. It gently demands that you abandon your cutlery and embrace a hands-on heritage.

We watched each other try it for the first time, taking a small piece, kneading it in the palm of our hand until it became a pliable little disc, and then shaping it into a scoop to catch the sauces.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Right beside it was a golden platter of Egg Fried Rice.
While not traditionally Zambian, it sat there like a gentle, familiar bridge between cultures.
Flecked with soft egg and savory seasoning, it provided a welcoming, neutral baseline that made the bold, exotic flavors around it feel right at home.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Stews That Tell a Story

The Oxtail was a masterclass in patience.

Slow-simmered for hours until the gelatinous meat literally dissolved off the bone at the touch of a finger, it was bathed in a rich, glossy, deeply savory reduction.

Pouring that luxurious gravy over the Nshima felt like a warm hug on a rainy afternoon.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

To balance the decadence of the meat, we passed around the bowl of Chilemba.

This hearty bean stew is a staple of Zambian home-cooking.

The sugar beans are boiled slowly with onions and tomatoes until they reach a velvety, melt-in-your-mouth texture, creating a thick, earthy broth that carries a subtle, natural sweetness. 

Image Source : BGOC Internal

The Green Canvas: Visashi and Rape

Zambian cuisine has a brilliant way of treating vegetables not as an afterthought, but as a highlight.

We fell in love with Visashi.

It’s a traditional dish where leafy green vegetables are stewed down in a rich, creamy sauce made from raw, pounded peanuts or groundnuts.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Next to it was Rape, which is savory, sautéed mustard greens.
Kept simple and flash-fried with just a hint of oil, tomatoes, and onions, it preserved its bright, peppery bite.
It acted as the perfect, crisp palate cleanser between the richer, heavier stews.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

New Textures That Sparked the Room

As a part of publication, we live for the moments that surprise us.

The real magic of the afternoon happened when we ventured into the authentic delicacies, turning our lunch into a playful sensory lab.

First was Kapenta.

These tiny, sun-dried fish from Lake Tanganyika were shallow-fried with onions and tomatoes until they achieved an immaculate, golden crisp.

Each bite delivered an intense, smoky burst of umami and a satisfying crunch that had us reaching back into the bowl like we were eating gourmet chips.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Next was Delele. This unique okra dish introduced us to a whole new texture.
Cooked with a touch of bicarbonate of soda to give it a wonderfully smooth, slippery, and viscous consistency, it is traditionally designed to help the dense Nshima slide down smoothly.
Image Source : BGOC Internal
Then came the true showstopper, the Vinkubala, which are sautéed mopane worms.
Seasoned perfectly and fried until crisp, they gave off a deeply earthy, nutty flavor with a distinct crunch.
Trying them became a beautiful test of shared courage for the team. 

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Why We Keep Exploring.

This lunch reminded us why we do what we do.

The best travel stories aren’t found by looking at a map from a distance.

Because, behind the KLTG desk, we are simply people who love the poetry of discovery. 

Until the next adventure,

From our family table to yours.

items.title: MY HERO ACADEMIA FINAL SEASON POP-UP STORE DEBUTS IN MALAYSIA AT SUNGEI WANG PLAZA
items.content:
Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Fans of My Hero Academia can look forward to an exciting new experience as the My Hero Academia Final Season Pop-Up Store makes its official debut in Malaysia. Organized by Medialink Group Limited (Medialink Malaysia), the limited-time activation will take place at Sungei Wang Plaza from 27 May to 17 June 2026.

Held in conjunction with the Malaysian school holiday season, the pop-up store offers fans an immersive retail and experiential journey inspired by the Final Season of the globally acclaimed anime series.


Event Highlights

Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Extensive Official Merchandise:

Explore over 100 SKUs of official merchandise, including newly released Final Season items and “Event Exclusive Only” items available in Malaysia for the first time. The collection caters to both dedicated collectors.

Explore over 100 officially licensed merchandise items on-site, including newly released Final Season collections and “event-exclusive” items making their debut in Malaysia. With a wide variety of products available, both dedicated collectors and casual anime fans will find something they love.

Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Immersive Themed Zones & Photo Opportunities

 The pop-up features a series of curated environments designed to bring the anime to life, including:

●      Plus Ultra Backdrop

●      Villain Zone

●      Pro Hero Photo Area

●      Class 1-A Graduation Photo Area

●      Final Season Scene Gallery

Fan Engagement Activation – Message Wall

 A dedicated Sticky Note Wall allows fans to leave messages, thoughts, and appreciation for the series, creating a collective tribute to the Final Season and its creators.

Interactive Game – Quirk Assessment Spin-to-Win

 Visitors can participate in a themed game experience at RM50 per play, where they can discover their “Quirk” and win exclusive prizes valued at up to RM120.

Gacha Collectable Card Series

An on-site gacha experience introduces a collectable card series, encouraging fans to build and expand their own hero collection.

Limited Edition Redemption

Shoppers who spend RM150 and above will be eligible to redeem a Limited Edition Holographic Laser Ticket, featuring key visuals from the Final Season showdown between Deku and Shigaraki.


Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Official Statement

“We’re excited to bring the Final Season experience of My Hero Academia to Malaysia for the very first time. Together with our venue partner, Sungai Wang Plaza, this pop-up is designed not just as a retail space, but as a place where fans can fully immerse themselves in the world of heroes, celebrate the series, and create memorable moments together,” said Vince Ng, Licensing Director of Medialink Malaysia.

Strengthening Malaysia's Anime Culture 

The debut of the My Hero Academia Final Season Pop-Up Store reflects the continued growth of anime fandom in Malaysia. It reinforces the country’s position as an emerging hub for anime & IP culture experiences. With its strategic timing during the school holidays, the event is expected to attract strong footfall from fans, families, and the wider public.


Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Event Details

●               Event: My Hero Academia Final Season Pop-Up Store

●               Date: 27 May – 17 June 2026

●               Venue : Sungei Wang Plaza (Venue Partner)

●               Organiser: Medialink Group Limited (Medialink Malaysia)

●               Media Partner: 8TV

  

About MY Hero Academia

My Hero Academia is a globally acclaimed Japanese anime series produced by Bones Inc., set in a world where the majority of the population possesses superpowers known as “Quirks.” The story follows Izuku Midoriya (Deku), a boy born without powers who rises to become a hero after inheriting the legendary ability “One For All” from the Symbol of Peace, All Might.

The anime chronicles Midoriya’s journey at U.A. High School alongside Class 1-A, as they train to become professional heroes while facing increasingly powerful villains led by Tomura Shigaraki. The narrative evolves from school life into large-scale conflicts that explore themes of justice, responsibility, and heroism.

The series features many iconic arcs and scenes, including the U.A. Sports Festival, the Kamino Incident (All Might vs All For One), Endeavour’s battle against the High-End Nomu, and the Paranormal Liberation War.

Now entering its Final Season, the story reaches its climactic conclusion, focusing on the decisive battle between heroes and villains, including the long-anticipated showdown between Deku and Shigaraki.

Widely recognized for its dynamic animation and strong storytelling, My Hero Academia remains one of the most influential anime titles worldwide.


About Medialink

Medialink Group Limited (Stock Code: 2230.HK) is a leading intellectual property (IP) management company headquartered in Hong Kong, with operations spanning China, India, Japan, and Southeast Asia. The Group is committed to promoting cultural exchange across the region through a diverse portfolio of IPs, delivering high-quality entertainment content to the Asian market. Malaysia serves as one of the Group’s key subsidiaries in Southeast Asia.

Founded in 1994, its business mainly focuses on content distribution and brand licensing, and is also involved in content production, distribution arrangements and animation product development. The Group invests and cooperates closely with media content licensors to distribute media content related to animation, variety shows, TV dramas, animated and live-action movies. At the same time, it also obtains copyright licensing from various brand licensors in the Asia-Pacific region, including merchandising rights, location-based entertainment rights and promotion rights.

The Group has its own animation brand, its various Ani-One® YouTube channels (including Ani-One® Asia, which is Asia-focused, Ani-One® 中文官方頻道, which is run in Chinese, and other Southeast Asia channels – Ani-One® Thailand, Ani-One® Philippines and Ani-One® Vietnam) have more than 5 million subscribers and more than 980 million views. In addition, the Group also has its own e-commerce platform, Ani-Mall®, selling animation products and an exclusive anime boutique.


About Sungei Wang Plaza

Sungei Wang Plaza positions itself as a beauty and experiential shopping hub in the heart of Kuala Lumpur with a variety of choices in Optical Services & Products.

Boutique Fashion & Fashion Accessories, Hair Salon, Beauty Salon, Manicure & Pedicure, Beauty Products, Athleisure, Entertainment, Digital Lifestyle, Toys & Hobbies, Art & Craft and Speciality Stores. For nearly five decades, Sungei Wang has been more than a shopping destination; it's been a cultural and community landmark in Kuala Lumpur. The mall has an aggregate retail floor area of approximately 800,000 square feet (sq. ft.) and key anchor tenants include Cold Storage, JUMPA@Sungei Wang, Blastacars, Camp5, MR DIY and Mega Star Arena Kuala Lumpur. Mega Star Arena Kuala Lumpur is a 5,000-capacity concert hall seamlessly integrated into the mall, captivating audiences with exceptional world-class concerts and events, solidifying its position as a vibrant hub within Bukit Bintang.

 

Sungei Wang Plaza has received many local and international awards and accolades over the years, including the Gold Award for Best Experiential Marketing by the Malaysia Shopping Malls Association (PPKM) Awards 2024-2025, Most Number of Optical Shops in a Shopping Mall by The Malaysia Book of Records, TripAdvisor Travelers’ Choice Award 2024, Special Award for Best Shopping Mall by the Mayor of Kuala Lumpur for Outstanding Lightings Design 2024, Silver Award for Best Experiential Marketing by the Malaysia Shopping Malls Association (PPKM) Awards 2023-2024, Leading Brand in Strata Title Mall awarded by The ASEAN Master Class Award in December 2023, the winner of the Best Managed Sustainable Property in the Retail category (10 years and above) awarded by The Edge Malaysia in July 2023, The BrandLaureate BestBrands Awards 2021-2022, Nation's Pride Brand of the Year in Nation's Most ICONIC & Renowned Mall, Kuala Lumpur Mayor’s Tourism Awards 2011 Award for Excellence in Shopping Mall Category and the prestigious FIABCI Prix d'Excellence under the Special Award (Retail Properties Category) in 1996. As Sungei Wang Plaza approaches its Golden Anniversary in 2027, it is poised to mark 50 years with even greater ambitions, aiming to redefine retail with a focus on innovation, sustainability, and community engagement. The vision is clear: to offer distinctive, unconventional experiences that captivate both new generations and loyal visitors alike.


Don’t just take our word for it—explore the vibrant floors of Sungei Wang Plaza this weekend and score your next favourite find.
